disclaimer: Companion syllabus checklist only -- not an official MIMIT exam and not an official HAREC certificate. Not legal advice.
not_legal_advice_ack: I understand this worksheet is not legal advice
source_note: Self-rated readiness against HAREC-aligned topic buckets. Re-check CEPT T/R 61-02 and current MIMIT pages before you sit any exam.

items.prompt: I can explain in my own words that national authorization is required for amateur transmit, and I opened the current MIMIT radioamatori pages.
I downloaded or opened the current CEPT T/R 61-02 PDF and listed the main syllabus topic groups I must study.
I can compute basic Ohm/power relationships and explain dBm vs watts without inventing exam numbers.
I can sketch a simple station (TX/RX, feedline, antenna) and name qualitative propagation ideas (LOS, ground wave, sky wave) without claiming invented distances.
I drafted a first-QSO cheat card with listen-first acknowledgement and phonetics for my practice string or callsign.
I keep the Chapter 2 field checklist and will not key RF with an unsafe antenna placement.
I can state why causing harmful interference is unacceptable and what I will do if someone reports that my experiment started a problem (stop, document, fix).
I wrote the current exam/portal steps from the official MIMIT site with an access date -- no invented fees or form numbers.
